text: Thanks for coming out. Jasper's been off on his front left since Saturday. He's a twelve year old Warmblood gelding, we do dressage.

speaker: dvm
text: Any change in shoeing, turnout or work before that?

speaker: client
text: The farrier came on Thursday. Otherwise nothing different.

speaker: dvm
text: His heart rate is forty, resp twelve, temperature thirty-seven point eight. Digital pulses are increased on the left fore.

speaker: dvm
text: At the trot he's a grade three out of five lame on the left fore. Hoof testers are positive over the toe of the left fore.

speaker: dvm
text: Flexion of the left fore is mildly positive. Right fore negative.

speaker: dvm
text: I'm going to pare the sole. There we go, that's a sub-solar abscess at the toe, and it's draining now.

speaker: dvm
text: I'll give him phenylbutazone, two point two milligrams per kilo IV today. Then poultice the foot daily for three days.

speaker: dvm
text: Continue bute by mouth, two grams once a day for three days. Keep him in a clean, dry stall.

speaker: client
text: He has a show in two weeks, is that okay?

speaker: dvm
text: Bute has a competition withdrawal, so check the rules for your show. If he's sound in a week, start light work. I'll recheck him on Friday.
